docs(spec): Phase-0 review response — authority reconciliation, F05 acceptance re-scope, provenance corrections (#566)

Two review rounds against #566's six acceptance criteria, no blockers.

Authority layer
- docs/DOCUMENTATION_POLICY.md source hierarchy admits docs/spec/ as the
  implementation-normative layer over technical-spec/ on concrete detail;
  docs/spec/README.md restates the identical scope so the two documents
  express one rule.
- GOAL_SPEC §3.1(2) no longer claims midgard-tx.md defines the resumable
  walk, Value bookmark, or Canonical-Data Acceptor. midgard-tx.md §1
  reserves §10 (#570) and §11 (#571) as deferred-by-design instead, so the
  by-reference binding stays honest without pre-empting Phase 3.

F05 manifest (AC6 re-scope half)
- Q00, C21, W27 and the CG2 gate row carry the amended GOAL_SPEC acceptance
  wording, each retaining its counted-scheme acceptance verbatim as
  provenance per invariant 14. 186 rows, id sequence byte-identical to
  b6e600f6, zero removals.

Provenance and numeric corrections
- §8.3 K basis and tier-1 bound re-sourced: the original text attributed
  both to #556/#557 observations that do not exist. Restated against what
  #556 actually measures, with a mandatory Phase-4 cross-check on K.
- GOAL_SPEC §3.3 no longer claims no verdict flips under the 13.2M basis:
  Q10 at 40 inputs (11,312,784) and Q11 at 41 (11,465,641) do sit in the
  11.2M-13.2M band and flip. Mitigation stated — the headline Q1X-F6 result
  at the admissible 296-input shape does not move.
- Epoch provenance separated: the captured artifact is decision 0001's
  Conway epoch-645 snapshot; epoch 648 is #552/#563 corroboration, not a
  captured artifact.
- decisions/0004 module counts re-derived against the tree (46 Aiken, 30 TS
  — the drafted 15 was wrong) with reproducing commands cited.
- §5.3 enumerates language_tag and purpose_tag admissible values against
  both language twins; 496-vs-512 reserve arithmetic reworded; tier
  vocabulary conversion completed across GOAL_SPEC.

Verified green: manifest-quality (PASS 186/186, 0 defects), fault-proof
reconciliation (70 rows/49 open), status-role control (PASS), CG4 gate
(BLOCKED unchanged from baseline), prettier --check on all changed docs.
Scope fence honored: no plutus.json, catalogue/deployment registry,
ABI-freeze artifact, or blueprint regeneration — those are reserved for
#579.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(spec): flat field-hash reversion Phase 0 — docs/spec authority, GOAL_SPEC amendment, decisions/0004

Phase 0 of the compact-tx flat field-hash reversion (#566; spec #565;
decision trail: wayfinder map #552, twelve closed tickets).

New authority layer. docs/spec/README.md states the rule: a component
spec wins over technical-spec/ on concrete detail, GOAL_SPEC binds it by
reference at scheme altitude, decision records carry rationale only.
docs/spec/midgard-tx.md is its first document — the implementation-
normative format authority for the MidgardTx compact types and canonical
encodings, the unchanged two-level tx-id derivation, the nine flat
blake2b-256 field commitments (plain hashing with a positional-identity
invariant), the uniform enveloped preimage grammar (counts only in the
preimage header; empty field = 80; per-item envelope now on all nine
fields including the newly enveloped 5/6/8), the fixed 3-byte output
index giving 38-byte spend/reference-input items at stride 40 with
arithmetic access, the asserted 28-byte observer/signer items at stride
30, the datum canonicity re-pin to serialiseData's image (#564), the
normative access invariants (authenticate-once, abort-never-clamp, count
consistency), and the three-tier carriage convention with
FieldPreimageCertificateV1 and the frozen FieldCarriageV1/FieldViewV1
wire types.

Provisional pins, marked provisional-pending-Phase-4-measurement, with
falsification an amendment-level erratum by design: K = 15,900 bytes
(the #556 case-3 measured two-chunk basis, 15,900 + 484 = 16,384) and
the tier-1 redeemer-carriage bound = 14,336 bytes (maxTxSize less a
2,048-byte step-machinery allowance). Tier-3 worst case is 3 chunks at
the retained 32,768-byte aggregate cap.

GOAL_SPEC amended at scheme altitude: §0 amendment note, §1 authority
list (new item 3; technical-spec 8 -> 9), §3.1(2), §3.2 ladder
re-derived as the three named tiers, §3.3 basis note declaring the
single 13,200,000-mem execution-budget basis (20% off live mainnet
maxTxExUnits 16,500,000, epoch 648), §8.2 preamble and C21/CG2, §9.1
output 3, §9.2 Q00, §10.3 W27, §12 (first-ever §12 edit, acknowledged
in place), §13.2 pointer, §13.3. Deliberate non-edits stated: DA payload
framing, MPF trie roots / mpf-chunked-verify, and the §3.3 thresholds.

Superseded-not-deleted per §3 invariant 14: 36 F05 manifest rows (Q00,
Q10-Q22, Q31, C20-0..C20-8, C21-C26, C29-C33, W27) now lead sourceAnchors
with a COUNTED-SCHEME SURFACE SUPERSEDED note, superseded text retained
verbatim as provenance. The Q1x Q10/Q11 output-5 cells are deliberately
NOT superseded — they stay OPEN until the Phase-7 re-measurement, since
the artifact is the honest gate.

Verification (all rerun after the manifest edit, per F05's
self-invalidation trigger): manifest quality gate 186/186 rows 0 defects;
fault-proof reconciliation 70 rows / 49 open; status-role control PASS;
CG4 gate exit 0; capability reconciliation 22 P2 tasks, 17 pass, 115/115
manifest-declared Aiken selectors across 12 modules under the pinned
aiken fork, 0 excluded. No gate state moved, as expected for a
docs-and-manifest-only change. Pre-existing red, unchanged on the
pristine tree and ticketed to the F40/F41 lane: the manifest quality

Refs #566, #565, #552, #561, #563

docs(goal): close the quiesce wave — DA-safety cluster complete, identity batch green

Q62 and all three Q63 clauses closed with measured gates; DA-INIT
compliance landed with the floors at the datum-writing seam; blueprint
regenerated (393 validators, dual-compiler byte-identical, sha256
70da64a3…9444); identity suites re-derive clean; deposit-flow 14/14
including the §4.4 journey against the new governor. The parent's
five invalid red runs (uncreated databases) are recorded as a
methodology defect with the checklist correction.

fix(node): scope DA governance floors to initialization, not config load

84bdbf2a enforced the Q63 governed floors inside `NodeConfig` loading.
That was the wrong seam. `DA_COMMITTEE_HEX`, `DA_OWNERS_HEX` and
`DA_THRESHOLD` are read by exactly one consumer — the bootstrap in
`deriveOperatorDaParams` — but `NodeConfig` is loaded by every subsystem,
so a stale deployment value failed config load for the whole process.

A checkout carrying the pre-Q63 `DA_THRESHOLD=1` in its `.env` therefore
could not load config at all, and the failure surfaced as an opaque
Effect ConfigError inside tests and subsystems that never touch DA:

  Invalid data at : "DA_THRESHOLD must be at least 2 to satisfy the
  governed threshold floor, received 1"

Config load now validates only what is malformed regardless of policy —
non-hex, ragged element widths, and out-of-order or duplicate entries in
a packed set, which the governor's `sorted_unique_*` walkers reject
outright. The governed floors stay fail-closed in `deriveOperatorDaParams`,
the one place a governor-invalid datum would actually be written, where
the real committee length is known even when it is derived from local
signers rather than configured — a case config load could never see.

No backdoor: a below-floor threshold, a one-member committee, and a lone
owner are all still refused, and are now pinned by an explicit regression
for the pre-Q63 `DA_THRESHOLD=1` shape. `tests/da-config-load.test.ts`
pins the other half — that those legacy values load without bricking
unrelated subsystems.

fix(da): adapt apply-flow consumers to the governed-params reference and close the Q63 gate

Q62's ApplyToStateQueue now carries da_params_ref_input_index and the
SDK apply builder requires the governed params; the node apply program,
the da-committee-node coordinator builder/submitter, and the watcher
indexer fixture adopt it in lockstep. The Q63 gate's three open-group
self-test fixtures re-point to strike their target group wherever it
lives (groups or openGroups) so none can no-op now that the rescue
groups closed; gate exits 0 with all nine groups measured (29 checks)
and the self-test still rejects every seed. Q62 manifest counts
restated against the published vocabulary; quality 186/186.
feat(da): non-retroactive committee rotation and partial-attestation rescue (Q62 + Q63c)

fix(node): require floor-compliant DA governance at bootstrap

Q63 (F04 §4) gave the DA params governor threshold floors —
`da_threshold >= max(2, ceil(2*committee_len/3))` and
`update_threshold >= max(2, ceil(2*owner_len/3))` — which make a 1-of-1
committee and a lone owner unrepresentable. The node's bootstrap still
built exactly that forbidden shape: a single-key committee, a single
owner, and both thresholds hardcoded to one.

Bootstrap now emits at least two committee members and two owners, with
both thresholds defaulted to the governed floor. All bound arithmetic is
delegated to the SDK twins (`governedThresholdFloor`,
`daParamsFloorViolations`) so it cannot drift from the validator, and
both sets are emitted sorted-unique to match the governor's
`sorted_unique_*` walkers.

The second key is explicit configuration, never invented:
`DA_COMMITTEE_HEX`/`DA_OWNERS_HEX` name a real committee and owner set in
a deployment, while `DA_COSIGNER_SEED_PHRASE` gives dev and emulator
bootstrap a locally held second key so one process can reach a genuine
2-of-2. With neither present, initialization fails closed rather than
falling back to the shape the governor rejects. The same floors are
enforced at config load so a bad value is reported where it can be read.

Attestation signing follows: the hardcoded single witness at index 0 is
replaced by one genuine Ed25519 signature per locally held key, with the
signer index looked up in the on-chain committee rather than assumed.

Fixtures pinning 1-of-1 are lifted to floor-compliant shapes, including
the Scalus suite that evaluates a real AddSignatures body through the
actual Plutus validator — now a true two-signature attestation.

The blueprint is deliberately not regenerated here; this lands green
against the old committed governor, which accepts >=2-of-N too.
docs(goal): ledger the Q63 remediation rounds and restate the manifest counts

fix(da): pin the governor mint seam and correct the Q63 evidence wording

Second remediation round on the Q63 DA-governor work, closing the residuals the
adversarial review left open on 9cf8817e.

MINT SEAM (load-bearing). The spend seam got a differential pair last round;
the mint path's own `valid_datum` call, in `params_output_datum_at_script`, did
not. That is the call the parent handoff's claim rests on when it says the
node's single-key DA defaults are now unmintable, and deleting its `expect`
left all 12 selectors green. It now has the same differential pair: an
initialisation transaction whose minted datum sits on the F04 floor is
accepted, and the identical transaction - same `init_ref` input, same single
minted NFT, same script output - differing only in a bare-majority
`da_threshold` of 3 over the 6-member committee is rejected. The control
passing is what establishes every other check in the handler is satisfied, so
the minted datum's governed floor is the only bound left to fail.
Mutation-confirmed: with that `expect` removed, exactly 1 of 14 fails; before
this round, 0 of 12 did.

COMPILER PIN. The gate now resolves the compiler from MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN then
MIDGARD_FORK_AIKEN_BIN - the precedence the Q60 verifier and the
capability-reconciliation gate use, since CI pins only the latter - and fails
closed with ERR_AIKEN_BINARY_UNPINNED only when neither is set. Whichever
resolves must report an `aiken v1.1.23` version or the run fails closed with
ERR_AIKEN_COMPILER_MISMATCH, so the stock v1.1.22 build cannot execute these
tests under the fork's name. Neither claim is left as an assurance: both are
seeded self-tests that spawn this gate's real main path, one with both
variables stripped and one against a stub binary reporting a v1.1.22 version.
The measured version is persisted into the artifact summary as
`aikenCompiler`, recomputed from the binary on every run.

HONEST WORDING. No full-table on-chain claim survives, because no full-table
Aiken sweep exists. The on-chain pins are widened to a genuinely adversarial
sample - the clamp boundary at 3 and 4, and the top of the range at 100, 255
and `max_indexed_signer_count` - and every description now says what it is:
full-table off-chain (digest over 0..256), sample-pinned on-chain. The SDK
docstring that claimed cross-language agreement over the whole range is
corrected to distinguish the two depths. The drain section comment claimed all
three owner bounds reject `test_params(6, 4, 1, 1)`; `update_threshold <=
owner_len` is in fact satisfied there, so it now states the two that reject and
explains why picking a different threshold only trades one violation for
another. The `no_threshold_satisfies_floor` docstring no longer asserts its
inequalities are `valid_datum`'s - it is arithmetic that mirrors their shape.
`floorTable.note` now says the digest's authority is the verifier's independent
recomputation and that `expression` is free-text documentation. The prose-only
"hash byte-identical" assurance is replaced by `reviewRemediationByteIdentity`,
which records the method (temp-directory A/B builds that never write the
repository's plutus.json), the observed hash and length, and states plainly
that this gate does not re-derive it and the parent must re-verify at the
identity batch.

HARDENING. A cited Vitest title that is a substring of another cited title is
now rejected (ERR_AMBIGUOUS_VITEST_CITATION): the runner match is
substring-tolerant by design, so one executed test could otherwise satisfy two
citations. A group id declared twice within `groups` or within `openGroups` is
rejected (ERR_DUPLICATE_GROUP_ID) instead of being silently deduped last-wins,
which would have left the earlier declaration's cardinality unchecked. Group
totals are published per language rather than collapsed to the first, so a
divergence between the two measured sides cannot hide behind one figure.

Both new guards carry their own seeds. The gate now runs 22 negative self-test
seeds and 3 positive controls, all spawning itself and observing its real exit
code.

The governor's validator code remains unchanged. The only non-test,
non-comment edits to da-params-governor.ak across both rounds are the
`transaction.{NoDatum, placeholder}` imports the test fixtures need; the
compiled `da_params_governor` mint/spend/else hash is byte-identical to
98975333 (f00f70a2a4a2de25ae2c52a5919195386067d3c1f2b3799965ef8352, 4448
chars), re-measured on this tree by A/B build.

test(state-queue): kill the interval-membership mutant and true up the Q60 evidence

The Q60 family claimed to prove that a committed header's `end_time` must EQUAL
the commit transaction's inclusive upper bound, "not merely be a member of the
interval". Measured, it proved no such thing: all 21 of its fixtures placed
`end_time` AT the bound or beyond it, so replacing the rule's equality with
interval membership (`lower <= end_time <= upper`) passed every one of them.
Three published boundaryClasses claims asserted an exclusion the family did not
have.

`commit_bound_header_time_is_valid` is correct and is NOT touched here. This
changes tests and evidence only.

Measured mutation experiment (patched fork aiken v1.1.23+2a78108; two scratch
copies of onchain/aiken outside the worktree, identical but for the predicate):

  pre-remediation family + mutant    collected 21, passed 21, failed 0
  remediated family + mutant         collected 23, passed 21, failed 2
  remediated family + real rule      collected 23, passed 23, failed 0

The two failures under the mutant are exactly the two tests added here.

On-chain fixtures added (onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/state-queue.test.ak):
- state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_an_end_strictly_inside_the_commit_window
  end_time 1_700_000_479_000 in window [1_700_000_000_000, 1_700_000_480_000]:
  satisfies `lower <= end_time <= upper` and must still be rejected.
- state_queue_commit_end_time_never_accepts_any_value_inside_the_window
  interior sweep at lower+1, the midpoint, and upper-1.

Off-chain (demo/midgard-node/tests/commit-block-header-state-queue-tail.test.ts):
every prior case used validTo-1, validTo+1 or far-future, all of which a `<=`
mutant of `headerEndTime === BigInt(validTo - 1)` also satisfies. Added a
strictly-below case (1_700_000_479_000) and an interior sweep. 10 tests -> 12.

Conjuncts removed, and why each proved nothing:

state_queue_commit_end_time_maximum_accepted_keeps_queue_and_merge_live
  - `1_700_605_280_000 >= 1_700_000_480_000 + block_maturity_duration_v1`
  - `!(1_700_605_279_999 >= 1_700_000_480_000 + block_maturity_duration_v1)`
  - `2_015_360_480_000 + block_maturity_duration_v1 > 1_700_605_280_000`
  The preceding conjunct pins `block_maturity_duration_v1` to 604_800_000, and
  that constant is the only symbol in all three. Once the pin holds, each is a
  comparison between two closed-form integers -- the first is literally `x >= x`
  -- so none can fail unless the pin already failed. Replaced with a second real
  call to `commit_bound_header_time_is_valid` over the next consecutive window,
  so the "queue keeps advancing" claim is asserted against something that moves.

state_queue_commit_end_time_bound_keeps_a_future_deposit_not_due
  - `commit_bound_header_time_is_valid(1_700_000_000_000, 1_700_000_480_000, ...)`
    byte-identical to
    state_queue_commit_end_time_maximum_accepted_is_the_inclusive_upper_bound
  - `!commit_bound_header_time_is_valid(1_700_000_000_000, 2_015_360_480_000, ...)`
    byte-identical to state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_a_far_future_end

state_queue_commit_end_time_bound_keeps_a_future_withdrawal_not_due
state_queue_commit_end_time_bound_keeps_a_future_forced_event_not_due
  - the same far-future rejection call, byte-identical to
    state_queue_commit_end_time_rejects_a_far_future_end

  A duplicated call on an identical fixture adds no failure mode the original
  does not already have. No coverage is lost: every removed disposition is still
  asserted once, against the real predicate, by the named dedicated test.

The three due-event tests now execute only their mirror conjuncts, and their doc
comments and artifact claims state plainly that they document the D-S12 harm
model over LOCAL MIRRORS of module-private predicates and do NOT execute
proof.ak.

Evidence artifact:
- the three membership-asserting claims now name the witness selector rather
  than asserting the exclusion themselves, and carry membershipExclusionWitness
- new strictlyInsideWindowRejection boundary class and
  vector.strictlyInsideHeaderEndTimeMs
- new mutationExperiment block recording both arms plus the pre-remediation arm
- blueprintImpact.verifiedBy no longer cites `git diff --stat` over
  onchain/aiken/plutus.json, which is gitignored (onchain/aiken/.gitignore:8)
  and untracked, so no diff could ever have witnessed it. It now states the
  honest basis: the code-bearing diff over validators/, lib/, env/ and
  aiken.toml excluding *.test.ak is empty (measured), nothing imports
  state_queue.test, and the blueprint is an untracked build artifact.

Verifier: REQUIRED_AIKEN_SELECTORS and REQUIRED_VITEST_TITLES are named in the
gate rather than read out of the artifact, so the killing fixtures cannot be
dropped later without failing it. Added ERR_Q60_NO_INTERIOR_CASE, the
mutationExperiment shape assertions (two arms, mutant fails, real passes, counts
total), and three new seeded self-test defects.

Verification: state_queue selector 23/23 collected/passed (was 21/21); vitest
12/12 (was 10/10); Q60 gate PASS with 17/17 Aiken selectors and 12/12 Vitest
tests; self-test 8/8 seeded defects rejected with their specific diagnostics;
`tsc --noEmit` clean; normalized Aiken format PASS; stock `aiken check
--skip-tests` 0 errors.
docs(goal): ledger the wave-1 quiesce lanes and the held identity batch

fix(da): pin the governor spend seam and harden the Q63 evidence gate

Closes the ten findings from the independent review of the Q63 DA-governor
work (98975333). Each was checked against source before being fixed, and the
two that turned on a claim about dead code were settled by mutation rather
than by reading.

E1 (evidence integrity). The gate's incompleteness signal was self-declared:
`evidence.openGroups` alone drove the non-zero exit, so deleting the two OPEN
entries turned it green with zero rescue paths measured. The verifier now
holds REQUIRED_GROUPS - the acceptance group set, each group's cardinality,
and the languages it must be carried in - and asserts every required id
appears in groups union openGroups with its expected count. A clause may be
recorded OPEN with its blocker; it may not be dropped, shrunk, duplicated, or
replaced by an invented one.

D1 (coverage). All eight tests called the private `valid_datum` directly, so
dropping `expect valid_datum(...)` from `params_output_datum_at_address` left
every one of them green. Two new tests drive the real `spend` handler through
a built Transaction: a quorum-signed continuing output below the floor
rejects, and its control - the same transaction differing in exactly one
field, `da_threshold` 5 instead of 3 - is accepted. Because the control
passes, every other check in the handler is satisfied, so the negative can
only be failing on the continuing output's governed floor. Mutation-confirmed:
with the `expect` removed, exactly 1 of 12 fails; before, 0 of 8 did.

E3 (arithmetic provenance). Quoting F04 proved the record still said what Q63
cited, not that anything computed it. The verifier now recomputes
`max(2, ceil(2n/3))` from a quotient-and-remainder integer ceiling -
deliberately not the `(2n+2)/3` form both implementations share - sweeps
0..max_indexed_signer_count, hashes the table, and asserts a digest published
in the artifact. A new Vitest check hashes the table produced by the SDK's
`governedThresholdFloor` and asserts the same digest, and reads
`max_indexed_signer_count` out of the Aiken source rather than restating it.
Three independently written computations now have to agree.

E2 (measurement). `vitestChecksExecuted` summed declared title counts and
never read the outcomes map. It is now derived from the titles the runner
reported as executed and passing, and a title cited twice is rejected so one
executed test cannot be counted for two claims.

D2/D3 (dead line). DECISION: keep `expect owner_len >= min_owner_count`, with
corrected comments and a renamed test. The review is right that it is
redundant, and mutation confirms it - removing the line leaves all 12 tests
green, because a one-owner set already fails `update_threshold >= floor(1)
== 2` against `update_threshold <= owner_len == 1`. It is kept because that
redundancy is an artifact of the current arithmetic, not a property of the
governor: F04 section 4's two-thirds term is an economic parameter, and if it
were ever weakened (say to `ceil(set_len/2)`, whose value at 1 is 1) a
one-owner set naming `update_threshold == 1` would become representable and
single-key governance capture would return. The line blocks that whatever the
floor becomes, which is worth more than deleting it. What was actually wrong
was the prose: the comments now say redundant-today defense in depth instead
of presenting it as THE drain protection, the false "each rejection pins
exactly one disposition" section comment is corrected, and the drain test is
renamed `..._rejects_owner_set_drained_to_one_by_overlapping_bounds` because
the overlap is not removable - every `update_threshold` a one-owner set could
name is either below the floor or above the owner count.

D4/D5 (overclaiming comments). The invariant docstrings now say they pin the
floor arithmetic and name what pins the datum wiring instead; "agree on every
set size" now reads "every representable set size".

D6 (twin drift). The SDK mirrors the on-chain split: MIN_DA_GOVERNED_THRESHOLD
clamps the threshold, MIN_DA_OWNER_COUNT bounds the owner set.

E7 (compiler identity). The gate fails closed with ERR_AIKEN_BINARY_UNPINNED
when MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN is unset - test execution is fork-only - spawns that
binary explicitly instead of the env default, and publishes its self-reported
version in its output.

I2 (consequence). A one-member DA committee is unrepresentable at any
threshold. Recorded in the artifact and pinned by two single-disposition Aiken
tests: an exhaustive non-`fail` search over every representable threshold
(preferred over `fail` across a conjunction), and one `fail` datum whose only
violable bound is `da_threshold <= committee_len`.

E5 (self-comparison). `summary` is rebuilt from measured runner results;
`acceptanceComplete` is derived from the required-group table rather than from
`openGroups.length`; genuinely declarative fields moved under `declared` and
are published as declarations checked against verifier-side constants.

Every new guard carries a hostile seed that proves it rejects: 19 negative
self-test seeds (9 pre-existing runner seeds, 9 new artifact-mutation seeds
including the exact dropped-OPEN-group defect, and the unpinned-compiler seed)
plus 3 positive controls, all spawning this gate and observing its real exit
code.

The governor's validator code is unchanged. The only non-test, non-comment
edit to da-params-governor.ak is importing `transaction.placeholder` for the
test fixtures; the compiled `da_params_governor` mint/spend/else hash is
byte-identical before and after
(f00f70a2a4a2de25ae2c52a5919195386067d3c1f2b3799965ef8352, 4448 chars), so
plutus.json does not move again on this commit.
